title: 10 Exercises for Balance and Fall Prevention // Full Follow Along Workout

method.teacher_system: The teacher introduces a balance and fall-prevention routine using a chair or wall for support. She guides learners through slow, controlled movements targeting hips, glutes, and thighs while emphasizing posture, core engagement, and breathing.
method.signature: Using a chair as a consistent base of support while deliberately moving through slow, controlled weight-transfers and balance exercises.

practices.what: Lift heels to shift weight onto the balls of the feet and lower down slowly.
Slow march, lifting one knee at a time in a controlled manner.
Flamingo balance position, lifting the leg behind, pulling it up to the knee, and opening out to the side.
Tandem stance with one heel directly in front of the other toe.
Side leg lifts holding onto a chair to work the outer glute muscles.
Wide stance squats with weight in the heels to strengthen inner thighs.
Donkey kicks with bent knees and flexed feet to target the gluteus maximus.

adaptations.adjustment: Have a chair, countertop, or wall as a base of support
Choose whether to wear shoes or go barefoot to feel the muscles in your feet

adaptations.difficulty: Maintaining balance while lifting a knee
adaptations.adjustment: Hold the chair and look over to the side while balancing
Keep arms out to the sides or hold onto the chair for support
Stay near a wall to use as a base of support
Hold onto the chair for support if needed

beliefs.belief: Going barefoot allows you to better feel the muscles working in your feet.
Some days are better than others, and your balance will improve with practice over time.

struggles.theme: Realizing poor balance or feeling wobbly during exercises
Deceptively harder than it looks, especially walking heel-to-toe
Recovering from recent falls, injuries, or surgeries
Dealing with chronic conditions like fibromyalgia or dizzy spells

clicked.theme: Appreciates the slow tempo, soft voice, and lack of bubbly energy
Noticeable improvement in balance after doing the routine regularly
Convenient to do anywhere, including offices or while wearing pajamas at home

requests.theme: Asks for more workouts and routines

meant.theme: Helps all age groups, from teens to seniors in their 80s and 90s, stay strong and stable

method.limits: Only the first 10 minutes of the video were analyzed; any subsequent cooldown or stretching was not captured.
